text:
maria: Quick heads-up — finished a cross-region throughput sweep for the new 6B quantized reranker+embed combo. Targets: dims 512/768, batch sizes 1/4/8/16, compare GPU int8 kernels vs CPU AVX2 fallback across us-west1, eu-west1, ap-south1. Results below.

bench-bot: summary (p95 latency / qps / notes)
- us-west1 (A100) int8-kernel-v2: 42ms p95 / 350 qps @ dims512/batch8
- eu-west1 (A10G) int8-kernel-v2: 58ms p95 / 240 qps @ dims512/batch8
- ap-south1 (T4-ish, older PCIe): GPU int8 fallback to scalar kernels -> 120ms p95 / 120 qps @ dims512/batch8
- ap-south1 (cpu-only nodes, 48 vCPUs, AVX2): 95ms p95 / 140 qps @ dims512/batch8
:chart_with_upwards_trend: TL;DR: APAC GPU instances underperform due to PCIe/driver/kernel mismatch; CPU fallback actually beats GPU for small batch sizes in that region.

ajay: whoa — CPU > GPU in ap-south1? that's unexpected. did you confirm NUMA binding and pinning?

maria: yes, ran the usual `--pin-cpus --numa-bind` flags. Weird part: PCIe lane speeds on the APAC instances are PCIe 3 rather than 4 and driver older, so the GPU spends extra time on KV cache transfers at each step. That kills p95 for small batches.

kelvin: can you paste the exact run command and kernel selection config?

maria: pasted snippet:
```
./run_bench --model rerank-6b-int8 --dims 768 --batch 8 \
  --kernel-policy prefer:int8-kernel-v2,fallback:scalar 
  --pin-cpus --numa-bind --region ap-south1 
  --warmup 300 --duration 1800
```

maria: kernel logs showed repeated fallback: `kernel_select: int8-kernel-v2 failed -> scalar_fallback` (driver 470).

yun: on quality — ran evals on the standard rerank testset (5k queries). int8 drops NDCG@10 by 2.3% vs fp16 for dims=768, but dims=512 shows only 0.6% drop.

ajay: so quantization impact is dim-dependent. maybe force dims512 for production in APAC?

maria: my recommendation:
- For US/EU: use GPU int8-kernel-v2, batching 8 for dims512, 16 for dims768 for best cost/latency.
- For APAC (older GPU hosts): either prefer CPU nodes for steady p95 at small batch sizes, or upgrade instance SKU to PCIe4 GPUs.
- Add a routing policy: region=ap-south1 -> model_variant=int8-dim512 or fallback=cpu-int8 to avoid p95 regression.

kelvin: capacity sizing notes?

maria: rough numbers (safety factor 1.3):
- us-west1: 6 x A100 pods per 1k incoming qps (dims512, batch8).
- eu-west1: 9 x A10G pods per 1k qps.
- ap-south1: 10 cpu-fallback nodes per 1k qps (or 12 old-gpu pods if not upgrading).

yun: also flagged a small regression in rerank correctness for one query family when using per-channel rounding — filed eval ticket EVAL-1221 with examples.

ajay: can the runtime auto-fallback to CPU only for requests above 90th percentile latency? we should avoid user-facing tail spikes.

maria: we have a quick policy prototype: `fallback_policy: p95_latency>80ms -> route: cpu-reserve(2)` — will dogfood for a day.

bench-bot: posted artifacts: https://artifacts.internal/redwood/bench/1938456789/plots.zip (contains latency histograms, per-region qps charts, kernel fallback traces).

kelvin: perfect. I'll take kernel/driver follow-up with infra. yun — can you add the eval diffs to the ticket and mark regressions that block int8 rollout?

yun: on it, adding eval details now.

maria: thanks — plan is: short-term routing + CPU fallback in APAC, medium-term host upgrades + kernel patch, long-term keep int8 for dims512 globally if evals OK.

ajay: sounds good. :thumbsup:

maria: one more note — microbatching set to 2 improved p50 significantly but didn't touch p95. so batching is useful for throughput but not for tail latency caused by kernel fallback.

kelvin: logged infra ticket INFRA-759 for APAC SKU review.

bench-bot: thread closed for now, will reopen if new artifacts appear.
